title: HMAC accumulation buffer cleared with XMEMSET not ForceZero — compiler may elide
description: Three call sites zero the Crypto2DevHmacCtx.data accumulation buffer with XMEMSET instead of ForceZero: (1) crypto2dev_hmac done: label (line 1218: XMEMSET(ctx->data, 0, ctx->dataCap)); (2) crypto2dev_free_hmac (line 1317: XMEMSET(ctx->data, 0, ctx->dataCap)); (3) crypto2dev_hmac_setkey_ctx on old_ctx replacement (line 1057: XMEMSET(old_ctx->data, 0, old_ctx->dataCap)). XMEMSET on a heap buffer about to be XFREE'd can be elided by the optimizer (dead store elimination). The accumulation buffer holds all HMAC input data, which in TLS contexts may include handshake messages or application data. After XFREE, the heap block may be reallocated and the prior content readable. ForceZero is not subject to dead-store elimination (it uses a volatile write). Fix: replace the three XMEMSET(ctx->data, ...) calls with ForceZero(ctx->data, ctx->dataCap).
